We need to find the maximum sum of a balanced subsequence.

Problem: given array nums[0..n-1]. A subsequence with indices i0 < i1 < ... < ik-1 is balanced if for each j≥1:

nums[i_j] - nums[i_{j-1}] >= i_j - i_{j-1}. Equivalent to: nums[i_j] - i_j >= nums[i_{j-1}] - i_{j-1}.

Let's verify: rearrange inequality:

nums[i_j] - nums[i_{j-1}] >= i_j - i_{j-1}
=> nums[i_j] - i_j >= nums[i_{j-1}] - i_{j-1}.

Thus condition is: The transformed values a_i = nums[i] - i must be non-decreasing along the subsequence.

Because we need a_i >= previous a_{prev}.

Thus we need to select a subsequence where a_i is non-decreasing (i.e., a_{i_j} >= a_{i_{j-1}}), maximizing sum of nums[i_j] (original values). Equivalent to: maximize sum of nums[i] subject to the sequence of a_i being non-decreasing.

This is reminiscent of weighted longest non-decreasing subsequence (LNDS) where weight is nums[i] (can be negative), we need max sum subsequence where a_i is non-decreasing. This is like DP: dp[i] = maximum sum of a balanced subsequence ending at index i (including i). Then dp[i] = nums[i] + max{ dp[j] | j < i and a_j <= a_i } (or dp[i] can be just nums[i] if none). Answer = max_i dp[i].

We need O(n log n) solution for n up to 1e5. So we need to maintain a data structure that can query maximum dp for all a_j <= current a_i. Since a_i can be any integer (range -1e9 - index ~ -1e9 to maybe +1e9+1e5). So we need coordinate compression of a_i values. Use Fenwick tree (BIT) or segment tree for max.

Implementation steps:

- Compute a_i = nums[i] - i for each i.

- Collect all distinct a_i, sort, assign index (1-based) for BIT.
